title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Any Director, the CEO, any KMP member, and any Employee nominated from time to time by the Chair or CEO to be a Restricted Person (which may include any Employee who reports directly to the CEO, has access to monthly management reports, or any other Employee whatsoever). This is the tier carrying the notice and Closed Period approval regime.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of APE. A subset of Restricted Persons, additionally subject to the 3 business day relevant-interest notification, the minimum shareholding requirement and the Margin Loan Board approval and disclosure regime.

tiers.name: KMP
tiers.description: Key management personnel as defined in the ASX Listing Rules. Restricted Persons, and subject to the minimum shareholding requirement alongside Directors.

tiers.name: Senior Executive
tiers.description: Any Employee nominated from time to time by the Chair or CEO to be a Senior Executive for the purpose of section 8 (Margin Loans). Relevant only to the Margin Loan approval and disclosure regime.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Any employee of APE or its subsidiaries. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, the improper use of position clause and, if a participant in an employee equity or incentive plan, the hedging restriction on unvested or trading-restricted plan Securities.

tiers.name: Related Party
tiers.description: Any person, company or other entity under the direct or indirect control of a Director or Senior Executive. Named only in the Margin Loan clause, which bars taking out a Margin Loan 'either personally or through a Related Party'. The dealing, notice and approval clauses are not expressly extended to associates.

definitions.hedging_definition: hedge or otherwise reduce or eliminate the risk associated with the plan by Dealing in derivatives, hedging or similar arrangements in relation to Securities that have not vested or are subject to trading restrictions under the plan

windows.start_anchor: 30th June (described in the policy as the end of APE's half year)
windows.end_anchor: announcement of results for that period or the giving of market guidance on the results

windows.start_anchor: 31st December (described in the policy as the end of APE's full year)
windows.end_anchor: announcement of results for that period or the giving of market guidance on the results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: No express power to impose additional or ad hoc blackouts. The Chair or CEO may, however, nominate any Employee to be a Restricted Person 'from time to time' and 'for the purpose of any provision of this policy', which can extend the notice and Closed Period approval regime to a person at any time; the policy does not say whether such nominations are confidential.

rules.detail: There is no express derivatives rule for vested unrestricted holdings. Securities is defined to include options, rights, warrants, forward contracts or tradeable financial products in respect of shares, with no venue limitation, and Deal means buy, sell, transfer, hedge or otherwise trade. An OTC put and written call are therefore a Dealing: outside Closed Periods it requires only prior notice to the Chair or Company Secretary, and during a Closed Period prior written approval of the Chair (or a non-executive Director for a Dealing by the Chair).
rules.evidence: Securities means shares or options, rights, warrants, forward contracts or tradeable financial products in respect of shares. ... Deal means buy, sell, transfer, hedge or otherwise trade.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options over APE shares are treated identically to OTC derivatives; the definition of Securities draws no distinction by venue and the policy contains no separate exchange-traded carve-out.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not Deal in APE Securities outside Closed Periods without prior notice to the Chair or Company Secretary (or in their absence, to a non-executive Director).

rules.detail: Dealing in derivatives over unvested plan Securities in order to reduce or eliminate plan risk is expressly caught, but is subject to the Chair's approval rather than being an absolute ban. Breach triggers forfeiture or lapsing of the unvested Securities, or the imposition of additional performance hurdles or trading restrictions, at the Board's discretion.
rules.evidence: Any Employee who participates in an employee equity or incentive plan must not hedge or otherwise reduce or eliminate the risk associated with the plan by Dealing in derivatives, hedging or similar arrangements in relation to Securities that have not vested or are subject to trading restrictions under the plan, without the Chair's approval.

rules.detail: The same clause expressly extends to plan Securities that are vested but 'subject to trading restrictions under the plan', so a collar over holding-locked shares needs the Chair's approval in addition to the Restricted Person notice or Closed Period approval.
rules.evidence: in relation to Securities that have not vested or are subject to trading restrictions under the plan, without the Chair's approval.

rules.detail: Hedging of unvested plan Securities is not banned outright: it is prohibited only 'without the Chair's approval'. The test is functional, capturing any arrangement that reduces or eliminates the risk associated with the plan.
rules.evidence: must not hedge or otherwise reduce or eliminate the risk associated with the plan by Dealing in derivatives, hedging or similar arrangements in relation to Securities that have not vested ... without the Chair's approval.

rules.detail: Plan Securities that have vested but remain subject to plan trading restrictions are expressly within the hedging clause and may be hedged only with the Chair's approval.
rules.evidence: or are subject to trading restrictions under the plan, without the Chair's approval.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested, unrestricted shares (whether acquired on-market or delivered out of a plan free of restrictions) is not separately regulated. It is a Dealing because Deal expressly includes 'hedge', so it needs prior notice outside Closed Periods and prior written approval during a Closed Period, and must not occur while the person has Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Deal means buy, sell, transfer, hedge or otherwise trade.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure is a Dealing in Securities because Securities expressly includes forward contracts in respect of shares, so it requires prior notice outside Closed Periods and prior written approval during a Closed Period. If the structure is funded by a loan secured against APE Securities it must also clear the Margin Loan gate in section 8.
rules.evidence: Securities means shares or options, rights, warrants, forward contracts or tradeable financial products in respect of shares.

rules.detail: The policy contains no short selling prohibition and does not use the term. A short sale would still be a Dealing requiring notice or approval.
Securities lending is not mentioned and is not listed in the definition of Deal, although a lending transfer would arguably fall within 'transfer'.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over APE shares is a tradeable financial product in respect of shares and so a Dealing in Securities, requiring prior notice outside Closed Periods and prior written approval during a Closed Period.
rules.evidence: Securities means shares or options, rights, warrants, forward contracts or tradeable financial products in respect of shares.

rules.detail: Margin Loans are permitted with prior Board approval, personally or through a Related Party. A Margin Loan is defined broadly as any loan secured against APE Securities where the lender is protected from falls in the value of the Securities by a call right over those Securities. Any Margin Loan actually taken out, approved or not, must be notified to the Chair immediately, with irrevocable consent to any public disclosure the Board considers necessary.
rules.evidence: Any person who is a Director or Senior Executive must not, either personally or through a Related Party, take out a Margin Loan without the prior approval of the Board.

rules.detail: Identical regime to Directors: prior Board approval, immediate notice to the Chair on taking out the loan, and irrevocable consent to public disclosure. Senior Executive means any Employee nominated from time to time by the Chair or CEO for the purpose of section 8, so the population is discretionary.
rules.evidence: Any Director or Senior Executive who takes out a Margin Loan, whether or not in contravention of the foregoing provision, must give immediate notice of the Margin Loan to the Chair and irrevocably consents to any public disclosure in relation to the Margin Loan which the Board may deem necessary or appropriate from time to time.

rules.detail: Section 8 applies only to Directors and Senior Executives. An employee who is neither is not restricted from margin lending by this policy.

Granting security over APE Securities is not itself a Dealing (Deal means buy, sell, transfer, hedge or otherwise trade) and there is no general encumbrance clause. An encumbrance is regulated only where it forms part of a Margin Loan as defined, in which case prior Board approval and immediate notice to the Chair apply. Security granted to a lender that is not protected from falls in value by a call right over the Securities falls outside the definition and is not addressed.
rules.evidence: Margin Loan means any loan secured against APE Securities where the lender is protected from falls in the value of the Securities by a call right over those Securities.

rules.detail: No encumbrance, pledge or charge restriction applies to Employees who are not Directors or Senior Executives.

There is no general ban on secured financing. Only a Margin Loan as defined is caught, and it is permitted with prior Board approval plus immediate notice to the Chair and consent to public disclosure. The policy does not distinguish vested from unvested Securities as collateral and does not address forced sales by a lender.
rules.evidence: must not, either personally or through a Related Party, take out a Margin Loan without the prior approval of the Board.

rules.detail: Same Board approval and Chair notification regime as Directors; no other form of secured financing over APE Securities is restricted.
rules.evidence: Any person who is a Director or Senior Executive must not, either personally or through a Related Party, take out a Margin Loan without the prior approval of the Board.

rules.detail: The policy imposes no minimum holding period, no buy/sell window and no prohibition on short-term or speculative dealing.

financing_disclosure: Directors and Senior Executives; trigger: taking out a Margin Loan (whether or not Board approved); to the Chair; deadline: immediately
Directors and Senior Executives; trigger: taking out a Margin Loan; irrevocable consent to public disclosure as the Board deems necessary or appropriate from time to time

financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Yes. Each Director and/or KMP member must hold a relevant interest in APE shares to a value at least equal to the Company's annual base fee for non-executive Directors, subject to a 3 year transitional period or as determined by the Chair. The policy does not say whether hedged, collared or encumbered shares are excluded from the holding.

ASX Listing Rules (relevant interest notification and KMP definition)
exemption_authority: Distributed: the Chair (or a non-executive Director, and a non-executive Director for the Chair's own Dealing) may approve Dealings in a Closed Period, expressly taking account of financial difficulties, imminent financial commitments, injury or illness, natural disaster, legal or regulatory requirements, and sales to fund plan exercise or associated tax; the Chair may approve hedging of unvested or trading-restricted plan Securities; the Board may approve a Margin Loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Margin Loan means any loan secured against APE Securities where the lender is protected from falls in the value of the Securities by a call right over those Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is secured against APE Securities and the bank takes a call right over them, so it should be treated as a Margin Loan requiring prior Board approval, immediate notice to the Chair and consent to public disclosure, even though it is not a margin loan in the conventional sense.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Section 8 restricts only Margin Loans, and only for Directors and Senior Executives; there is no general prohibition on secured financing, encumbrance or hedging of vested shares anywhere in the policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies this one leaves a funded collar over vested unrestricted shares available, subject to Board approval of the loan and the ordinary notice or Closed Period approval for the derivative legs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Employee who participates in an employee equity or incentive plan must not hedge ... Securities that have not vested or are subject to trading restrictions under the plan, without the Chair's approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even unvested and holding-locked plan shares can in principle be collared with the Chair's approval, which is unusual; without approval the sanction is forfeiture or lapsing of the unvested Securities.

bespoke_clauses.topic: notice not approval outside closed periods
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not Deal in APE Securities outside Closed Periods without prior notice to the Chair or Company Secretary (or in their absence, to a non-executive Director).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering, rolling or unwinding the collar outside a Closed Period needs only prior notice, with no stated approval, validity period or response deadline, so execution timing is far more flexible than under a preclearance regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approval may include conditions include the period in which the Dealing may occur.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Closed Period approval for collar entry or settlement can be time-boxed or otherwise conditioned, so the bank should treat the approval terms as execution constraints.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The prohibitions on Dealing in Securities under clauses 3.1 and 3.2 will not apply to any Dealing ... in respect of which the Restricted Person has no control or influence over the Dealing decision.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale or a bank's physical settlement of the collar during a Closed Period is arguably outside the executive's control and so within this exception, but the policy nowhere addresses forced sales expressly and the point is untested.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Director and/or KMP member must hold a relevant interest in APE shares to a value of at least equal to the Company's annual base fee for non-executive Directors, subject to a transitional period to acquire the initial holding of 3 years.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares pledged under the collar still give a relevant interest, but the policy is silent on whether hedged shares count towards the MSR, so the size of the collar relative to the required holding should be raised with the Chair.

bespoke_clauses.clause: irrevocably consents to any public disclosure in relation to the Margin Loan which the Board may deem necessary or appropriate from time to time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The existence and terms of the collar loan may be publicly disclosed at the Board's discretion, which the executive cannot withdraw consent to, so confidentiality cannot be assured to the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Closed Period means any period from: (i) 30th June (ie. the end of APE's half year) until either results for that half year are announced ... or (ii) 31st December (ie. the end of APE's full year) until ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The half year and full year labels are transposed relative to APE's actual reporting calendar, but the operative dates are clear: 30 June and 31 December to results or guidance, and all collar entry, roll and unwind should be scheduled outside those two periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any Employee who is nominated from time to time by the Chair or CEO to be a Restricted Person for the purpose of any provision of this policy ... or any other Employee whatsoever.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A counterparty cannot rely on an executive's current status; the Chair or CEO can bring any employee into the Restricted Person or Senior Executive regime at any time, changing the approvals needed to unwind an existing collar.

summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable at Eagers Automotive, making this one of the more permissive ASX policies for this structure. Over vested, unrestricted shares the put and call legs are a Dealing (Deal expressly includes 'hedge' and Securities includes options and forward contracts in respect of shares), so a Restricted Person needs only prior notice to the Chair or Company Secretary outside the two Closed Periods (30 June and 31 December until results or guidance), or prior written and potentially conditioned approval of the Chair if entered inside one. The loan leg is the gating item: a loan secured against APE Securities where the lender is protected by a call right is a Margin Loan, which a Director or Senior Executive may take out only with prior Board approval, must notify to the Chair immediately, and is subject to irrevocable consent to public disclosure. Plan shares that are unvested or still subject to plan trading restrictions can be collared only with the Chair's approval, with forfeiture as the sanction for breach, so the cleanest structure uses vested unrestricted shares. There is no short-term trading ban, no short selling or stock lending prohibition and no general secured financing ban, but the Director and KMP minimum shareholding requirement and the silence on lender forced sales should be resolved with the Chair before execution.
